Separate reports warn of a potentially critical remote code execution flaw in OpenJDK, tracked as CVE-2026-114938. IT teams running Java SE should track the Oracle patch release.

items.headline: Amazon EMR 8.2 is now available
items.summary: Amazon EMR 8.2 is now available with new features across Amazon EMR on EC2, Amazon EMR on EKS, and Amazon EMR Serverless. This release upgrades Apache Spark to 4.1.3, Apache Iceberg to 1.11.0, and Delta Lake to 4.2.0, and it is designated a Long Term Support (LTS) release. This release makes it easier to run secure, governed analytics at scale — you can now write to the same Delta Lake table on Amazon S3 from multiple clusters concurrently, refresh Iceberg materialized views incrementally, and propagate end-user identity from Spark jobs and interactive sessions all the way to AWS Lake Formation and Amazon S3 so access is authorized and audited as the original user. Amazon EMR 8.2 expands gov
lines: Amazon EMR 8.2 is now available across Amazon EMR on EC2, Amazon EMR on EKS, and Amazon EMR Serverless.
The release upgrades Apache Spark to 4.1.3, Apache Iceberg to 1.11.0, and Delta Lake to 4.2.0, and is designated a Long Term Support (LTS) release.

New capabilities include concurrent writes to the same Delta Lake table on Amazon S3 from multiple clusters, incremental refresh of Iceberg materialized views, and end-user identity propagation to AWS Lake Formation and Amazon S3.
The release supports governed analytics at scale, with access authorized and audited as the original user.

items.headline: Amazon ECR now supports global authentication tokens for private registries
items.summary: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) now supports global authentication tokens for private registries. Previously, you needed to request a separate authentication token in each AWS Region where you push or pull container images. Now, you can request a single token from the AWS Sign-In CreateBearerToken API and use it across all ECR private registries in the same AWS partition. Teams that run proxy services to route container pulls across Regions, a common pattern for optimizing latency or availability, previously had to request, refresh, and coordinate a separate token for every Region behind the proxy. With global tokens, the proxy manages one token for all Regions in the AWS part
lines: Amazon ECR now supports global authentication tokens for private registries.
A single token can be requested from the AWS Sign-In CreateBearerToken API and used across all ECR private registries in the same AWS partition.
Previously, a separate token was needed in each AWS Region where images were pushed or pulled, which complicated proxy services that route pulls across Regions.

items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory now lets you keep short-term memory events for up to 10 years, up from one year. Developers can now use short-term memory as a long-lived record of agent conversations and interactions. This helps when that history needs to stay available for a long time, such as for compliance and audit, for users who come back after months away, or for agents that need to look back at past sessions. You set retention on the memory resource, and it's applied to each event when the event is created, so existing events keep their original retention. Standard short-term memory storage charges apply for as long as you keep the data. This feature is available in all AWS Regions wh
lines: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory now lets users keep short-term memory events for up to 10 years, up from one year.
Retention is set on the memory resource and applied to each event when it is created, so existing events keep their original retention.
Standard short-term memory storage charges apply for as long as the data is kept, which helps with compliance, audit, and agents that review past sessions.

lines: Amazon SageMaker now offers AI data preparation capabilities to build training and evaluation datasets for text-based model customization and traditional ML.

The feature targets the manual labeling and data cleaning work that has traditionally taken weeks.

items.headline: Amazon DynamoDB caching is now available with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey
items.summary: Today, AWS announces the general availability of DynamoDB caching with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey, enabling sub-millisecond read latency for frequently accessed DynamoDB data. Previously, if you required faster reads than DynamoDB's single-digit millisecond latency, you had to manually manage cache infrastructure or keep a separate cache in sync. Now you can access DynamoDB table data from a write-through cache that updates as data changes and automatically scales to meet changing workload demands. lines: AWS announced general availability of DynamoDB caching with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey.
It provides sub-millisecond read latency for frequently accessed DynamoDB data through a write-through cache that scales automatically.
No application logic changes are required, and users choose which tables and APIs to cache and how long to retain cached data.

items.headline: Rethinking Windows management for modern IT
items.summary: Windows management has always had a straightforward goal: keep people productive while keeping devices secure, current, and resilient. But the environment has changed. IT teams are managing more apps, more types of devices and workloads, and now AI agents. Adding another tool or process doesn't solve that challenge. It just gives IT one more thing to manage. Security updates add urgency to the equation. AI is changing the pace of vulnerability discovery for defenders and attackers alike. As that pace increases, reducing the time it takes to get available security updates onto devices becomes even more important. But moving faster can't mean giving up the testing, visibility, and control IT n
lines: A Windows management post says IT teams now handle more apps, device types, workloads, and AI agents, and that adding another tool or process does not solve this.
The post says AI is changing the pace of vulnerability discovery for both defenders and attackers, which raises the importance of getting security updates onto devices faster.
For IT teams, the post argues that faster update deployment should not come at the expense of testing, visibility, and control.
